## Kimchi CodeQL database

> **Last verified:** 2026-10-22 — Kimchi 1.17.2; `passthru.codeql` carries
> `database`, `databaseOf`, `runQueries`, `mkQueryRunner`, `createDatabase` and
> `engine`; the environment and network facts read it; explicit named lifecycle
> tasks publish checkout generations from the pinned derivation source.

### Three layers

`packages/kimchi/lib/codeql.nix`, reached through
`self.ciPackages.<system>.kimchi.passthru.codeql`:

- **`source`**, internal to the file: the tree `database` is created from, not a
  passthru attribute. It moves with the Kimchi or pi pins and with the flake's
  nixpkgs (stdenv, bash, jq, coreutils, patch).
- **`database`**: one CodeQL database of `source`, under `$out/db`. It moves
  with `source`, the engine and nixpkgs, so a nixpkgs bump costs one database
  rebuild of about 85 s.
- **`runQueries { name; queries; models ? []; on ? database; }`**: every query
  of an `ai.devTools.codeql.mkQueryPack` spec, run against a copy of `on` with
  optional `mkModelPack` specs. `engine.customizePackage` realizes the specs,
  compiling against the engine that built the database. `databaseOf name tree`
  builds a database of another tree laid out as `source`. `$out/<query>.json` is
  `codeql bqrs decode --format=json` of every result set of `<query>.ql`, its
  tuples sorted. `mkQueryRunner { queries; models; }` is the same run as a
  script, `kimchi-codeql-run-queries <db> <out>`.

Select strings, relative paths and numbers only: an entity or an absolute
location carries the build directory into the JSON. Every derivation name
contains `codeql`, so the credentialed cachix steps'
`pushFilter: kiro-cli|codeql` keeps all of them out of the public cache. The
`Assert no CodeQL engine or database is published` tripwire in `ci.yml` also
asserts 404 there for both databases, the release's and the network fixture's,
and for every other CodeQL derivation the network check needs. The database is
input-addressed and not bit-reproducible (`codeql-database.yml` records its
creation time). The Hestia check cache serves it again for as long as the pins,
the engine and the flake's nixpkgs stay the same.

### The source root

```text
kimchi/src/                              Kimchi's TypeScript, no *.test.ts, no __mocks__
kimchi/{package.json,tsconfig.json}
kimchi/node_modules/@earendil-works/<pi package>/{package.json,dist/}
```

- **Kimchi's GitHub release source, not the build's patched tree.** This is the
  tree `extract.mjs` reads, so a CodeQL fact and an `extract.mjs` fact describe
  the same code. This repository's packaging patches (`command-shell.patch`,
  `package-identity.patch`, ...) are not in it, and neither is Kimchi's upstream
  postinstall rewrite: `scripts/patch-pi-ai-oauth.js` replaces pi-ai's
  `dist/auth/oauth/oauth-page.js`, and `extract.mjs` does not apply it.
- **pi's four packages sit under `kimchi/node_modules`**, where Kimchi's imports
  resolve them. Measured: 506 of Kimchi's 508 `@earendil-works/*` import
  declarations resolve to a pi module in the database. The TypeScript extractor
  scanned only pi-coding-agent's dist, saw the other three as `index.d.ts` types
  and read patch `+` lines; the database holds all four `dist/` trees, patched.
  On 1.17.0 the environment fact is the same either way.
- **Kimchi's own `node_modules` (its pnpm store) is not in it.** That is every
  third-party dependency except what pi's bundle inlines (below).
- **Source maps are dropped:** 13.5 MB of pi's dist the extractor never reads.
- **The extractor skips `node_modules` by default.**
  `LGTM_INDEX_FILTERS=include:kimchi/node_modules/@earendil-works` brings pi
  back in: without it the database held none of pi's files. The value is a
  directory: an include ending in `/**` fails with `Illegal use of '**'`.

### Minified files

`pi-coding-agent/dist/bundle/` is pi's minified standalone CLI, which Kimchi
never loads. It is carried for the environment reads of pi's bundled third-party
dependencies (AWS SDK, Google auth, undici, ws) at pi's build-time versions: 48
of the 237 variables in the current environment fact are named in its chunks and
nowhere else in pi, Kimchi or its patches. It also holds unpatched copies of
patched pi-ai, pi-tui and pi-coding-agent code, so a query scopes or labels its
`dist/bundle` rows. The extractor skips a file it judges minified: without
`CODEQL_EXTRACTOR_JAVASCRIPT_ALLOW_MINIFIED_FILES=true` it skipped 46 files: 42
chunks, the three `dist/bundle` entry files (`cli.js`, `index.js`,
`rpc-entry.js`) and the vendored `marked.min.js`. The flag grows the 2.27.3
database, logs included, from 113 to 216 MB.

### The patch step

Kimchi's `package.json` `pnpm.patchedDependencies` names its pi patches
(pi-coding-agent, pi-ai and pi-tui at 0.85.1). Each one is applied to the
carried tree with `patch -p1 --fuzz=0`, as pnpm applies them in the build. A
patch for a pi package that is not carried, or for another version, fails the
build. Only these patches are in the database; `source` refuses another whose
added lines name `env` (kimchi-codeql-environment.md).

### The database is a directory

`query run` and `database run-queries` refuse a bundle
(`Database root ... is not a directory`), and a query writes its cache into the
database: a read-only one fails with `Error acquiring the IMB cache lock`. So
every consumer copies the database first. Measured locally on the 214 MB
database: copying the directory took 0.1 s, unzipping its 100 MB
`codeql database bundle` 1.3 s, and building that bundle 10 s. `$out/db` drops
the creation `log/`. `createDatabase`
(`kimchi-codeql-create-database <dir> [<tree>]`) copies `<tree>`, by default
`source`, to `<dir>/source` and creates `<dir>/db`; the derivation, the devenv
task and the environment guard all run it.

### Running a query without Nix

```bash
devenv tasks run codeql:kimchi:up        # once per pin
state=.devenv/state/codeql/kimchi
"$state/engine/bin/codeql" query run --database="$state/db" \
  --additional-packs=packages/kimchi/ql --output=/tmp/out.bqrs \
  packages/kimchi/ql/smoke/EnvReads.ql
"$state/engine/bin/codeql" bqrs decode --format=json /tmp/out.bqrs
```

The generic lifecycle uses the engine and creator store paths as its input
stamp, so changes to the pinned source, patch step or extractor environment
invalidate the database even without a version bump. `codeql:kimchi:refresh`
forces a new generation; `codeql:kimchi:down` removes this checkout's database.
`db` links to a complete generation, with `stamp` and `engine` beside it;
publication is atomic and failed extraction leaves the previous generation.
Resolve `db` for every query request. Result paths are relative to that
generation's `source/` tree. Existing databases refresh in the background after
a merge or branch checkout, with diagnostics in `refresh.log`. See
[the shared lifecycle](../../codeql/docs/codeql.md#local-database-lifecycle).

`packages/kimchi/ql/qlpack.yml` makes the whole directory one local pack, so a
`.ql` file anywhere under it resolves `import javascript`. A query file outside
any pack fails with `could not resolve module javascript`. Each subdirectory is
also one `mkQueryPack` source, which writes its own qlpack.yml, so a query
importing a sibling directory's `.qll` resolves locally but not through
`mkQueryPack`.

Measured with the smoke query on a 16-core x86_64-linux workstation: a cold
first run took 35 s, the same query again 5 to 10 s, an edited query 17 to 25 s
(about 15 s to compile). The Nix path compiles the pack first: 66 s in CI run
39642944093 for the codeql-customize checks' two-query pack.

### CI measurements

From the `checks (owner-kimchi)` job of run 39667792203 (2026-10-21, a 4-core
x86_64-linux runner, engine substituted from the check cache):

- `database` took 85 s (58 s of extraction with 4 threads, 23.5 s of TRAP
  import): 133.8 MiB of relations, a 56.0 MiB string pool, a 6.0 MiB archive.
- `runQueries` on the smoke pack took 9 s (5.7 s evaluation) for 362 rows.
- `mkQueryPack` compiled the smoke pack in 33 s, in parallel with `database`.
- The check cache's drain pushed the job's 11 built paths (85.6 MiB); run
  39670617753 copied the same database from it in under 2 s instead of building.

### Licence

The CodeQL Terms allow automated database creation only for an OSI-licensed
codebase hosted and maintained on GitHub.com. Kimchi is Apache-2.0 at
`github.com/getkimchi/kimchi`. pi is MIT at `github.com/earendil-works/pi`, and
the database reads its npm dist, which is built from that repository.

## The environment fact from CodeQL

> **Last verified:** 2026-10-22 — `environment.variables` comes from the
> `ql/environment` pack over the release database; its output is byte-identical
> to the fact the TypeScript extractor produced for 1.17.2; a fixture guard
> holds the shapes that extractor accepted and refused.

`extracted.json`'s `environment` surface is one fact the CodeQL database
produces. `extract/environment.nix` runs the two-query pack
`packages/kimchi/ql/environment/` through `runQueries` and
`extract/environment.jq` over the decoded result sets; `package.nix` splices
that surface into the raw `extract.mjs` writes. The engine builds on
x86_64-linux only, which is the one system every row of `extracted/facts.json`
declares, so `passthru.extracted` exists on that system alone and
`kimchi-extracted` wires no other host.

### What the queries answer

`EnvironmentReads.ql` lists every named read of `process.env` with the runtime
that reads it: `kimchi/src/**` is `kimchi`, every pi package under
`kimchi/node_modules/@earendil-works/` is `pi`. The process object is
`NodeJSLib::process()`, so the global under any name, `globalThis.process`, and
a default or namespace import of `process` all count, and local flow follows
aliases, `??` and `||` fallbacks, parameter defaults and
`const { env } = process`. A computed name is evaluated by a QL copy of the
extractor's `stringConstant`: literals, templates, `.toUpperCase()`, identifiers
followed through their declarators and ES imports (minified `export{a as K}`
included), and a by-name fallback for a constant with no reachable initializer,
two strata deep, that fails when same-named constants disagree. pi's `APP_NAME`
takes `kimchi/package.json`'s `piConfig.name`, as at runtime. `+` is not folded,
a `delete` operand is not a read, `+=` and `??=` are.

`LaunchOverwrites.ql` names the variables `entry.ts` fixes on every launch, by
the rules `launchOverwrites` applied: top-level statements in order, entering
blocks and both arms of an if with an else, for writes and their refusals alike;
writes through `process.env` spelled out only; reads in function declarations
and in functions handed `process.env` counted first, a parameter's computed key
evaluated like any other and refused when it cannot be; and a failure for every
shape that makes the order unknowable. "After it suspends" follows the
extractor's children-first walk by end position, not the control-flow graph,
which would accept `if (c) { await 0 } else { process.env.X = "1" }`.

Either query emits `fail` rows instead of guessing; the transform fails on any,
naming each, and the `extracted` build fails with it.

### Two shapes kept out on purpose

The extractor at 1.17.2 did not read `const { X } = process.env` or a read
through `import { env } from "node:process"`. The database finds both: seven
names, `GIT_*` from `src/extensions/work-attribution/scope.ts`, `HOMEDRIVE` and
`HOMEPATH`, and `AWS_EXECUTION_ENV` from the bundled AWS SDK. `tsIncompatible`
in `EnvReads.qll` drops them so the committed fact is unchanged. They are real
reads; deleting that predicate adds them, and `rules.nix` reconciles unannotated
non-secret names without a row. That is a data decision, not a bug fix.

The database also reads four shapes the extractor missed that 1.17.2 does not
use (`process["env"]`, `(process.env as T).X`, `require("process").env` and an
alias of `process` itself), misses one it read (the namespace binding of
`import d, * as ns from "node:process"`, a statement 1.17.2 does not contain:
measured when biome merged two fixture imports into one), and reads pi-ai,
pi-tui and pi-agent-core whole where the extractor saw their `.d.ts` and
Kimchi's patch lines. On 1.17.2 both make no difference; a later release may
gain a correct name from them.

### Annotations

`extract/annotations.json`'s `environment` and `environmentIgnored` are not an
input of the transform. `rules.nix` applies them downstream, against
`environment.variables.<name>`, as it always did.

### The guard

`kimchi-codeql-environment-guard` runs the pack and transform over each tree
under `checks/fixtures/codeql-environment/`, laid out like the real source root
and extracted by `kimchi-codeql-create-database <dir> <tree>`. `reads` holds
seven read shapes absent from the pinned tree in one Kimchi file: bracket `env`,
an asserted environment, a process alias, bracket `globalThis.process`, literal
`require("process")`, a namespace process import, and `+=`; concatenation
remains unevaluated. The pinned release's byte identity covers its actual read
shapes, including pi's APP_NAME and bundled imports. `overwrites` holds the
launch-order mix; `fail-shapes`, `fail-order` and `fail-sources` retain every
refusal assertion, with helper declarations merged into their case. A new shape
goes into one of these trees, not into a mutant of the real source: a real-tree
mutant costs a database build each.

### Running it without Nix

```bash
devenv tasks run codeql:kimchi:up        # once per pin
state=.devenv/state/codeql/kimchi
for q in EnvironmentReads LaunchOverwrites; do
  "$state/engine/bin/codeql" query run --database="$state/db" \
    --additional-packs=packages/kimchi/ql --output="/tmp/$q.bqrs" \
    "packages/kimchi/ql/environment/$q.ql"
  "$state/engine/bin/codeql" bqrs decode --format=json "/tmp/$q.bqrs" \
    | jq --sort-keys 'map_values(.tuples |= sort)' > "/tmp/$q.json"
done
jq -S -n -f packages/kimchi/extract/environment.jq \
  --slurpfile reads /tmp/EnvironmentReads.json \
  --slurpfile overwrites /tmp/LaunchOverwrites.json > /tmp/environment.json
jq -S .environment packages/kimchi/extracted/extracted.json | cmp - /tmp/environment.json
```

The fourth column of a reads row and the third of an overwrites row is the site,
`path:line`, for reading a result back; the transform ignores it. Measured on a
16-core x86_64-linux workstation: the reads query takes 27 to 90 s against the
1.17.2 database, the overwrites query about 30 s.

### Patches the tree does not carry

Kimchi patches the MCP SDK and client, pi-mcp-adapter and playwright-core too,
packages the source root does not carry, so the queries never see their added
lines. The extractor read them as text. `source` refuses an added line in one of
them that names `env`, with the fix: carry the package. Joining a patch's `+`
lines into a file does not work here: CodeQL drops a file with any syntax error,
and five of the seven joined patches had none of their code extracted.

## Kimchi network fact

> **Last verified:** 2026-10-22 — Kimchi 1.17.2; `network` is measured on
> x86_64-linux by `ql/network` with the `ql/models/{sdk,undici}` packs through
> `runQueries`; a modeled request is an invocation of its row's own callee and
> takes its library from that row; a host constant reaches a `hostname` by value
> flow; the fixture's minified chunk is one the extractor skips without the
> flag.
>
> **Settled — do not relitigate.** Each was measured on the 2.27.3 bundle and
> rejected:
>
> - **A `byFieldName` join** pairing each unreached `baseUrl` literal with every
>   SDK call site whose target reads `baseUrl`. It recovered 35 of pi's 71
>   catalog hosts, as a cross product: 47 literals by 6 call sites, 288 rows.
> - **A typeModel for esbuild's `__require`.** A models-as-data path starts from
>   a package or `global`, and `__require` is a module-local variable.

### The pipeline

`lib/network.nix` builds the query pack and the two model packs, runs them on
the release database with `codeql.runQueries`, and reshapes the result with
`lib/network.jq`. On x86_64-linux, the kimchi package's `passthru.extracted`
adds it to `extract.mjs`'s output as `network`. Every CodeQL fact joins there,
from `codeqlFacts`. Other hosts carry no CodeQL facts, and the declaration lists
x86_64-linux only. `extractedRules.results.network.entries` is the fact. The
regenerate command builds the database and runs the queries, so kimchi's update
script now does too on update.yml's runner, with no check cache: the engine
customization, the database, the pack compile (1m54s on CI) and an evaluation
with `--ram=8192` (53.8 s).

```text
{callSites: [{readBy, file, line, library, bundledModule,
              targets: [{kind, value, host, origin}]}],
 unattributed: [{readBy, file, line, value, host}]}
```

- **`readBy`** is `kimchi` or `pi`. **`file`** and **`origin`** are relative to
  Kimchi's tree (`src/...`) or to its `node_modules` (`@earendil-works/...`).
  **`line`** only: a minified chunk puts many call sites on one line, and they
  share a row per library.
- **`library`**: `fetch`, `node-http`, `websocket`, `axios`, `undici`,
  `sdk:<package>` for another modeled package, or `sdk:<class>` for a
  `new C({baseURL})` matched by option name, because a bundle inlines the SDK
  and its import is gone. Any such class matches, a non-client one included,
  except `new this.constructor({...})`, which names no class.
- **`bundledModule`**: the esbuild `__commonJS` key enclosing the call, such as
  `node_modules/undici/index.js`. It means a dependency pi inlined.
- **`unattributed`**: URL literals no call site reads. The regex-scan inventory
  stays in the fact, but these literals are not attributed to any call site.

### Target kinds

`url` is a string with a scheme, `host` a scheme-less host literal joined after
`://` or that is a target's whole value (`hostname: "h"`, or `hostname: HOST` by
value flow from `const HOST = "h"`), `env` a `process.env` read (its value is
the name). When none of them reaches any target, the target is classified
instead: `argument` (a parameter's name), `property` (a property's name) or
`dynamic` (the expression's text, which CodeQL truncates in the middle with
`...`). A target read from a Kimchi config key is `property` or `dynamic`: the
fact does not name the config path.

Origins are taint flow: an origin influences the target and is not proof that it
is the whole of it. A wrapper takes every caller's origins. Kimchi's
`src/utils/http.ts:90` (`fetchWithRetry`) carries 11 targets, from the regions
table, `src/update/github.ts` and the npm registry. Two flow steps
over-approximate. `ComputedKeyRead` reads every property for `REGIONS[region]`,
so one call lists both regions' hosts. `ObjectSpreadAlias` aliases each spread
operand, which is where `app.kimchi.dev` was lost before. Both are global
`AdditionalFlowStep`s, so they change any query that runs in the same
evaluation.

### Models, and why there is a bridge

The javascript library models global `fetch`, node-fetch, `http`/`https`,
WebSocket and `ws`, axios, got and others as `ClientRequest`. It has no undici
model at all (`grep -rln undici` over javascript-all 2.10.4 finds nothing). A
models-as-data row alone never makes a `ClientRequest`: `request-forgery` rows
only become `RequestForgery::Sink`s. `ModeledClientRequest` in
`ql/network/Network.qll` bridges them: an invocation of the callee a
`request-forgery` row names, whose argument or a member of it one or two levels
deep is that row's sink, becomes a `ClientRequest`. After that, a library needs
only rows. The sink alone is not enough: an options object handed to the SDK and
to a logger is one sink node, and both calls would match. For the same reason
`sdk:<package>` is the matched row's package, not one read from the sink.

- **`ql/models/undici`**: the `undici.Dispatcher` type (every agent, pool and
  client class, `getGlobalDispatcher`, `compose`), its per-call `origin`, the
  top-level `request`/`fetch`/`stream`/`pipeline`/`connect`/`upgrade`, the
  origin-bound constructors, the proxy URLs, and `EventSource`/`WebSocket`.
- **`ql/models/sdk`**: `openai`, `@anthropic-ai/sdk`, `@google/genai`, the
  Bedrock runtime client and the MCP transports. A package name containing a dot
  must be single-quoted inside the row
  (`"'@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/sse.js'"`). Unquoted, it matches nothing,
  without an error.

### Bundles and minified chunks

The release database already sets
`CODEQL_EXTRACTOR_JAVASCRIPT_ALLOW_MINIFIED_FILES=true` (`kimchi-codeql.md`).
Without it the extractor skips 46 pi files, which include every bundle chunk.
The bundle is minified without renaming identifiers, so the global `fetch` still
matches by name. esbuild's own module shapes are not imports. Two
`ModuleImportNode::Range`s cover them: `__require("https")` and
`__toESM(require_x())` of a `__commonJS({"node_modules/<pkg>/...": ...})`
factory. Each matches the helper under its own name or as an imported alias.
They must be `overlay[local?]` and syntactic only, or compilation fails with
`Declaration is annotated overlay[local] but depends on global entity`. Other
bundlers (Bun's compiled kimchi binary, rollup, webpack) would need their own
ranges.

### What the fact does not reach

pi's provider catalog (`groq_default={...baseUrl:"https://api.groq.com/..."}`)
reaches its SDK clients only through runtime model selection. Those URLs stay in
`unattributed`, and the SDK call sites read `property baseUrl`. Go
(`tools/proxy-helper`) is outside a javascript database.

### The fixture check

`kimchi-codeql-network` builds a database of `checks/fixtures/network` with
`codeql.databaseOf`, which lays it out as the release tree, so `readBy`, the
`node_modules` include and the minified flag hold too. It requires the fact's
rows to equal `checks/fixtures/network-expected.txt`. That file has one line per
target. The source cases share one file, with a separate module for the local
`fetch` negative; the three bundle chunks retain helper and minified shapes. Its
negative controls are a docs-only URL, a browser-only URL, a module-local
`fetch` in `src/` and in the minified chunk, and
`new this.constructor({baseURL})`. Each must appear only as an unattributed
literal. A host constant joined into a URL's path is no host. Options objects
also handed to `console` or an imported logger must yield the SDK's row and not
the logger's, and one handed to two SDKs a row per SDK, each with its own
package. `chunk-minified.js` averages over 200 characters a line, so the
extractor skips it without the flag (measured: files averaging 173 were kept,
231 skipped), and its 5 rows go. The expected lines name fixture line numbers,
so reformatting a fixture file means regenerating them. biome leaves the chunks
under `node_modules` as they are.

### Running it without Nix

`codeql:kimchi:up` creates the database, and the query loop in
`kimchi-codeql.md` can then run `ql/network/NetworkCallSites.ql` on it, without
the model packs. The pack directories have no qlpack.yml, as `mkModelPack`
writes it. For the full rows, give CodeQL one model pack holding both
directories' `*.model.yml`, with `library: true`,
`extensionTargets: {codeql/javascript-all: "*"}`, `--additional-packs` and
`--model-packs`, as `customizePackage` does. Measured locally with 6 threads:
the query compiled in 93 s and evaluated on the release database in 51 s.
